title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not Grothendieck's own writing. It is a typed English page, numbered 4, with "25" added by hand. It is evidently part of a typescript expounding Dennis Sullivan's theory of minimal models (c. 1973–77), kept among Grothendieck's notes for his 1976 IHÉS talk on the divided-power de Rham complex.

The mathematics is the first two stages of the inductive construction of a Sullivan minimal model for a commutative differential graded algebra E over a field of characteristic 0.
- Hypotheses: E is homologically connected (H^0 E = k) and has first Betti number zero (H^1 E = 0, the simply connected case).
- Step 1: Take the free graded-commutative algebra Λ(x_1,…,x_n) on degree-2 generators with d = 0. Map x_i to cocycles ρ_1 x_i whose classes form a basis of H^2 E. Then ρ_1 is an isomorphism on H^2. It is trivially injective on H^3, since Λ(x) has nothing in degree 3.
- Step 2: Adjoin degree-3 generators of two kinds.
  - y_1,…,y_ℓ with dy = 0, mapped to cocycle representatives of a basis of H^3 E. This kills the cokernel of ρ in H^3.
  - y_{ℓ+k} with dy_{ℓ+k} = Σ a^k_ij x_i x_j, where these quadratic polynomials form a basis of ker(H^4 ρ_1). Since ρ_1 of each such element is exact in E, one can choose ρ_2(y_{ℓ+k}) with d ρ_2(y_{ℓ+k}) = Σ a^k_ij ρ_1(x_i) ρ_1(x_j).
- Result: ρ_2 is an isomorphism on H^≤3 and injective on H^4.
  - Degree 4 of Λ(x;y) is still S^2⟨x⟩, all of it cocycles, and the new coboundaries are exactly the kernel.
  - The new degree-3 cocycles are only the span of y_1,…,y_ℓ, because the dy_{ℓ+k} are linearly independent.
- Continuing degree by degree gives the minimal model. The text then announces the comparison with the rational Postnikov tower of a simply connected space X, with E the de Rham (or polynomial-forms) algebra.

Why it is in this file: the next page, in Grothendieck's hand, develops integration on simplicial differential graded groups. He proves existence and uniqueness of maps K_n : A_n^n → A_0 satisfying a Stokes formula; this is the abstract form of the Sullivan / Bousfield–Gugenheim simplicial de Rham theorem. So Grothendieck was studying Sullivan's rational homotopy theory as background or motivation for an integral (divided-power) analogue of the polynomial de Rham complex.
errors: Typo in Step 2: 'to make ρ_1 surjective on cohomology in dimension 3' should read ρ_2 (the extended map).
'ρ_1x_1,…,ρ_1x_n generate H^2E' should say they form a basis (or are cocycles whose classes form a basis). Otherwise ρ_1 is not injective on H^2, contradicting 'isomorphism'.
Finite dimensionality of H^2, H^3 and of the kernel is tacitly assumed: 'rank of H^3' and finite indices n, m. In general one needs possibly infinite bases.
E must be a commutative DGA over a field of characteristic 0 for the free commutative algebra Λ to map multiplicatively. This is implicit.
Unbalanced parenthesis '(Now ρ_2 is …'. This is cosmetic.

ideas.what: Inductive construction of a minimal model Λ(x_i; y_j; …) → E for a simply connected commutative DGA, by adjoining generators degree by degree to kill cokernel and kernel on cohomology
ideas.usually_credited_to: D. Sullivan (Infinitesimal computations in topology, Publ. IHÉS 1977; earlier lectures 1973–75); also Deligne–Griffiths–Morgan–Sullivan 1975
ideas.where_published: Sullivan, Publ. Math. IHÉS 47 (1977); Bousfield–Gugenheim, Mem. AMS 179 (1976)

ideas.what: Relation of the minimal model to the rational Postnikov tower of a simply connected space via the de Rham algebra
ideas.modern_name: Sullivan's equivalence between rational homotopy types and minimal models
ideas.usually_credited_to: Sullivan; Quillen (1969) for the Lie model

missed.claim: Archival/historical point only: Grothendieck kept, alongside his 1976 notes on the divided-power de Rham complex, an exposition of Sullivan's minimal models. His adjacent handwritten page develops a simplicial Stokes/integration theorem. This documents that his integral de Rham project was framed against Sullivan's rational theory. Integral or divided-power versions of polynomial forms were later pursued by others (e.g. Cenkl–Porter). Nothing mathematically new is on this page itself.
missed.quote: At this point one can show by a standard Postnikov argument how this construction relates to the homotopy theory of a simply connected space X.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of interest for the history of integral and p-adic models of homotopy types (divided-power de Rham, E∞ cochains of Mandell). It is not a new result.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a standard typed exposition of Sullivan's minimal model construction, not by Grothendieck. It is only mildly interesting as evidence of what he was reading for his divided-power de Rham talk.
transcription_corrections: The page is typewritten in English (not Grothendieck's hand), page-numbered '4' with a handwritten '25'. It is a different document from the surrounding manuscript pages.
The boxed passage ('where ℓ is the rank of H^3E … kernel ρ_1 on 4-dimensional cohomology') is enclosed by a hand-drawn dashed frame in the original, suggesting an insertion or emphasis.
